question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
The availability of funds will be / ensured if they all tried to / submit the proposals on time.
option_1: The availability of funds will be
option_4: ensured if they all tried to
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ensured if they all tried to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence is a Conditional Sentence (Type I / First Conditional), which expresses a real or highly probable future condition and its result.

• Rule — Conditional Sentence Type I: If + Subject + V1/V5 (Simple Present), Subject + will/shall + V1 (Simple Future). Both clauses must maintain a consistent present-future pairing; a past tense verb like "tried" cannot appear in the "if" clause when the main clause uses "will be ensured".
◦ Correct pattern: If they all try to submit the proposals on time, the availability of funds will be ensured.

• In the given sentence, the main clause "The availability of funds will be ensured" is in the Simple Future Tense, so the "if" clause must be in the Simple Present Tense. The verb "tried" (past tense) is therefore incorrect and must be replaced by "try".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "The availability of funds will be" — this segment is grammatically correct; it correctly uses the future tense "will be" to match the main clause.

• Option 2: "No error" — incorrect, because an error does exist in the sentence (as explained above).

• Option 3: "submit the proposals on time" — this segment is correct; it is simply the infinitive phrase completing "tried to", and carries no grammatical fault of its own.

NOTE

• In conditional sentences, examiners frequently test tense-mismatch errors between the "if" clause and the main clause — always check that both clauses belong to the same conditional type (Type 0, I, II, or III).

• Common confusable pairs tested in SSC error-spotting: "if he comes" vs "if he came" (Type I vs Type II), and "would have" vs "will have" in mixed conditionals.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A person who does not believe that God or Gods exist.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Atheist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "Atheist" is a person who does not believe in the existence of God or gods. (नास्तिक)
◦ Example: As a committed atheist, he rejected all forms of organised religion.

• The word comes from the Greek "atheos", meaning "without god" ("a-" = without + "theos" = god).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Irreverent (अनादरपूर्ण): Showing a lack of respect for people or things that are generally taken seriously; not necessarily related to disbelief in God.

• Option 3: Profane (अपवित्र): Showing disrespect for God or sacred things, or having a secular (non-religious) character; not the same as denying God's existence.

• Option 4: Blasphemous (ईशनिंदा से युक्त): Showing contempt or lack of reverence for God through speech or action; again, distinct from simply not believing in God.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions often confused with "Atheist": "Agnostic" — a person who believes that the existence of God can neither be proved nor disproved; "Theist" — a person who believes in the existence of God; "Pantheist" — one who believes God is present in everything in the universe.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Sharp practice
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Dishonesty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Sharp practice" means dishonest or barely legal dealings, especially in business or trade. (बेईमानी/छल-कपट से भरा व्यवहार)
◦ Example: The company was accused of sharp practice after cheating several clients out of their investments.

• The phrase suggests conduct that is technically within the letter of the law but ethically dishonest or deceptive.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Frequently — means happening often; unrelated to the idiom's meaning of dishonesty.

• Option 3: Briefly — means for a short time; not connected to the idiom.

• Option 4: Nearby — means close by in location; has no connection to dishonest dealing.

NOTE

• Other idioms of dishonesty/deception often asked in SSC: "Play foul" (to cheat), "Have an axe to grind" (to have a hidden selfish motive), and "Above board" (honest and open, the opposite of sharp practice).

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. But the question that perturbs Ruskin's mind is what social pressure can be exercised against a dishonest person.
B. The merchant, for instance, must supply perfect and pure things to the people.
C. Ruskin believes that in every civilised society there exist five intellectual professions, namely the soldier, the pastor, the physician, the lawyer and the merchant.
D. Persons belonging to these professions are expected to perform their duty honestly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. CDBA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence C is the clear opening line — it introduces the topic (Ruskin's belief about five intellectual professions in a civilised society) and must come first, since B, A and D all depend on this introduction.

• Sentence D logically follows C, as it states the general expectation (honest duty) that applies to the professions just listed in C.

• Sentence B then gives a specific example (the merchant) to illustrate the general expectation of honesty stated in D.

• Sentence A concludes the paragraph, shifting from the example to Ruskin's underlying question about social pressure on a dishonest person — a natural conclusion after the merchant example.

• Reading the paragraph in order: C → D → B → A gives a coherent, logically flowing passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 (CDBA).

Additional Information

• Option 1 (BACD) is incorrect because it opens with the specific example (the merchant) before the general introduction of the five professions has been made, which is illogical.

• Option 2 (DABC) is incorrect because it opens with the expectation of honest duty before the professions themselves have even been introduced.

• Option 4 (ABDC) is incorrect because it opens with Ruskin's concluding question before any context about the professions has been given.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always identify the sentence that introduces the subject/topic (usually contains a proper noun or a general statement) — this is almost always the opening sentence, and sentences containing pronouns like "these", "this", "he", "it" usually cannot open the paragraph as they refer back to something already mentioned.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. But she has no idea an aunt and uncle are waiting for her.
B. 'The Strange Child' is the story of a young girl who believes she is the only one on the planet.
C. Her parents simply vanished into thin air one day.
D. She travels the world in search of Nevada because she aspires to reside in the Mojave Desert.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. BCDA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence B must open the paragraph, as it introduces the title and the protagonist of the story — "'The Strange Child' is the story of a young girl who believes she is the only one on the planet."

• Sentence C follows naturally, explaining why the girl feels alone — her parents vanished one day.

• Sentence D then describes the resulting action she takes — travelling the world in search of Nevada, aspiring to live in the Mojave Desert.

• Sentence A concludes the sequence with the contrasting twist introduced by "But" — she is unaware that an aunt and uncle are waiting for her — which can only make sense after her journey (D) has been mentioned.

• Reading in order: B → C → D → A produces a coherent narrative.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 (BCDA).

Additional Information

• Option 1 (DABC) is incorrect because it opens with the girl's journey before the story and its protagonist have even been introduced.

• Option 2 (BDAC) is incorrect because it places the contrasting sentence A (about the aunt and uncle) before C, which breaks the logical cause-effect link between the parents vanishing (C) and her journey (D).

• Option 3 (BACD) is incorrect because it introduces the twist about the aunt and uncle (A) before explaining why she is alone (C) and where she travels (D), disrupting the narrative flow.

NOTE

• In narrative para-jumbles, look for connector words like "But", "So", "Therefore" — sentence A here begins with "But", signalling a contrast that must follow the point it contrasts with (her journey/search), so it is very unlikely to be an early sentence.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Did you not buy the return tickets to Dehradun?
option_1: Was the return tickets to Dehradun not bought by you?
option_2: Were the return tickets to Dehradun not being bought by you?
option_3: Had the return tickets to Dehradun not bought by you?
option_4: Were the return tickets to Dehradun not bought by you?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Were the return tickets to Dehradun not bought by you?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Did you not buy the return tickets to Dehradun?" is a negative interrogative sentence in the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense (Negative Interrogative):
◦ Active: Did + Subject + not + V1 + Object?
◦ Passive: Was/Were + Object + not + V3 + by + Subject?

• Applying the rule: the object "the return tickets to Dehradun" becomes the subject of the passive sentence; since "tickets" is plural, the auxiliary used is "Were"; the verb "buy" becomes the past participle "bought"; and "you" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: Were the return tickets to Dehradun not bought by you?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "Was" is used with the plural object "tickets"; it should be "Were".

• Option 2 is incorrect because "not being bought" wrongly changes the tense to a continuous form, which does not correspond to the Simple Past Tense of the original sentence.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "Had ... not bought" is the passive structure of the Past Perfect Tense, not the Simple Past Tense used in the question.

NOTE

• Remember: in negative interrogative Simple Past passive constructions, the auxiliary (was/were) always agrees in number with the new subject (the former object), not with the original subject.

question:
In the following sentence, four words are underlined, out of which one word is incorrectly spelt. Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
Seema was a timid girl. She did not talk to people who were not familiar to her. She was an introvert since adolosense.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. adolosense.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "adolescence" — the period of life between childhood and adulthood. (किशोरावस्था)
◦ Example: Many personality traits develop during adolescence.

• Spelling key: A-D-O-L-E-S-C-E-N-C-E. Note the "sc" combination (not "s" alone) and the ending "-ence" (not "-ense"). The word "adolosense" wrongly spells it with "o" instead of "e" after "adol", and "-sense" instead of "-scence".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "introvert" — correctly spelt; a person who is shy, reserved, and more focused on their own thoughts than on the outside world.

• Option 2: "timid" — correctly spelt; means easily frightened or lacking courage/confidence.

• Option 4: "familiar" — correctly spelt; means well known or easily recognised.

NOTE

• Other commonly misspelt "-ence/-ance" words tested in SSC: occurrence, existence, maintenance, resemblance, correspondence, coincidence.

• Remember the related word "adolescent" (noun/adjective, the person going through adolescence) is spelt with the same "sc" pattern.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom/phrase that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Vennela made a big fuss about a small problem.
option_1: Get a taste of your own medicine
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A storm in a teacup.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "A storm in a teacup" means a great deal of anger, excitement or worry about a matter that is actually trivial or unimportant — i.e., making a big fuss about a small problem. (तिल का ताड़ बनाना)
◦ Example: The argument over the seating arrangement turned out to be just a storm in a teacup.

• The imagery is of a "storm" (turmoil) confined within the small space of a teacup — dramatic in appearance but insignificant in scale.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Get a taste of your own medicine (जैसे को तैसा): To be treated the way one has treated others, usually badly.

• Option 2: Barking up the wrong tree (गलत जगह प्रयास करना): To pursue a mistaken course of action, based on faulty reasoning.

• Option 3: Add insult to injury (जले पर नमक छिड़कना): To make a bad situation even worse for someone, especially by saying or doing something hurtful.

NOTE

• Other idioms meaning "to exaggerate a trivial matter" often asked in SSC: "Make a mountain out of a molehill" (very close synonym of "a storm in a teacup") and "Much ado about nothing."

question: Describe how you will tell your parents that Mahesh and his team were helping the fire and rescue team in passive voice.
option_1: The fire and rescue team helped by Mahesh and his team.
option_2: The fire and rescue team was being helped by Mahesh and his team.
option_3: The fire and rescue team being help by Mahesh and his team.
option_4: Mahesh and his team were been helping the fire and rescue team.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The fire and rescue team was being helped by Mahesh and his team.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Mahesh and his team were helping the fire and rescue team" is in the Past Continuous Tense.

• Rule — Past Continuous Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + was/were + V-ing + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the fire and rescue team" becomes the subject (singular, so "was" is used); the verb "helping" becomes "being helped"; and "Mahesh and his team" becomes the agent introduced by "by".
◦ Passive: The fire and rescue team was being helped by Mahesh and his team.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "helped" without an auxiliary is not a valid passive verb form for the Past Continuous Tense; the auxiliary "was being" is missing.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "being help" uses the base form "help" instead of the past participle "helped", and the auxiliary "was" is also missing.

• Option 4 is incorrect because it keeps the sentence in the active voice with the faulty structure "were been helping", which is grammatically wrong and not a passive construction at all.

NOTE

• A common trap in passive-voice questions is confusing the tense of the object with the tense of the original subject — always check the number (singular/plural) of the new subject (the former object) to select "was" or "were" correctly.

question:
Select the grammatically correct statement from among the given options.

A. It is a nice party. I am enjoying the party.
B. It is a party. I am enjoying an party.
C. It is party. I am enjoying a party.
D. It is the party. I am enjoying an party.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence A — "It is a nice party. I am enjoying the party." — is grammatically correct: the indefinite article "a" is correctly used before "nice party" (introducing it for the first time), and the definite article "the" is correctly used the second time, since the same, now-specific, party is being referred to again.

• Rule — Articles: Use "a/an" when a noun is mentioned for the first time or is non-specific; use "the" when referring back to a noun already mentioned or when the noun is a specific, particular one known to both speaker and listener.

• Rule — "a" vs "an": Use "a" before words beginning with a consonant sound (e.g., "a party") and "an" before words beginning with a vowel sound (e.g., "an hour"). Since "party" begins with a consonant sound, "an party" is always incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 (A).

Additional Information

• Option 1 (D) is incorrect because "an party" wrongly uses "an" before the consonant-sound word "party"; it should be "a party".

• Option 2 (B) is incorrect for the same reason — "an party" should be "a party" — and it also fails to use the definite article "the" on second reference.

• Option 3 (C) is incorrect because the first sentence, "It is party", is missing the required article "a" before the singular countable noun "party".

NOTE

• A singular countable noun (like "party") can never stand alone without an article ("a/an" or "the") in standard English — this is a very common SSC error-spotting and sentence-improvement trap.

• Also remember: "an" is used before vowel sounds, not just vowel letters (e.g., "an hour" — silent 'h'; but "a university" — 'u' sounds like 'yoo', a consonant sound).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A book or set of books giving information about all areas of knowledge
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Encyclopedia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "Encyclopedia" is a book or set of books giving information about many different subjects, or about many aspects of one subject, usually arranged alphabetically. (विश्वकोश)
◦ Example: She looked up the topic of volcanoes in the encyclopedia.

• The word derives from the Greek "enkyklios paideia", meaning "well-rounded education" or "general knowledge".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Dictionary (शब्दकोश): A book that lists words in alphabetical order along with their meanings, pronunciation, and usage — not general knowledge across all subjects.

• Option 3: Volume (खंड): A single book, especially one of a series or set; a general term for a book, not specifically one containing all-round knowledge.

• Option 4: Anthology (संकलन): A published collection of poems, stories, or other pieces of writing, usually by different authors on a related theme.

NOTE

• Commonly confused reference-book substitutes in SSC: "Thesaurus" (a book of synonyms and antonyms), "Almanac" (an annual publication with statistics/calendar information), and "Glossary" (an alphabetical list of terms with definitions, usually at the end of a book).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Peruse
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Check.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Peruse" means to read or examine something, typically in a careful and thorough manner; in everyday usage it is also loosely used to mean "to check/look over". (ध्यान से पढ़ना/जांचना)
◦ Example: The manager perused the contract before signing it.

• Among the given options, "Check" (to examine something in order to determine its accuracy or condition) is the closest in meaning to "peruse".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Draw (खींचना): To produce a picture or diagram, or to pull something; unrelated in meaning to reading/examining.

• Option 3: Pursue (पीछा करना): To follow or chase someone/something, or to continue with a course of action; this is a commonly confused near-homophone of "peruse" but has an entirely different meaning.

• Option 4: Narrate (वर्णन करना): To tell a story or give a spoken account of something; not the same as reading/examining a text.

NOTE

• "Peruse" and "Pursue" are a classic pair of confusable words in SSC vocabulary questions due to their similar spelling — always remember "peruse" relates to reading/examining, while "pursue" relates to following/chasing.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. We often make all things around us the way we want them.
B. Even during our pilgrimages, we have begun to look for whatever makes our heart happy, gives comfort to our body and peace to the mind.
C. Our mind is resourceful enough to find shortcuts in simple and easy ways.
D. It is as if external solutions will fulfil our needs, and we do not want to make any special efforts even in our spiritual search.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. CABD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence C opens the paragraph, introducing the general idea that the mind is resourceful enough to find shortcuts — this sets up the topic developed by the rest of the paragraph.

• Sentence A follows, giving a general application of this idea — that we make things around us the way we want them.

• Sentence B narrows the idea to a specific context — even during pilgrimages, we seek comfort and happiness — extending the point made in A.

• Sentence D concludes the paragraph, summarising the underlying attitude — that we expect external solutions to fulfil our needs without making special efforts, even in spiritual matters.

• Reading in order: C → A → B → D forms a logical, coherent paragraph.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 (CABD).

Additional Information

• Option 2 (ADBC) is incorrect because it opens with a specific application (A) before the general idea about the resourceful mind (C) has been introduced.

• Option 3 (ABDC) is incorrect because it places the concluding, summarising sentence D before C, disrupting the logical build-up of the argument.

• Option 4 (DABC) is incorrect because it opens with the concluding sentence D, which makes no sense without the context established by C, A and B first.

NOTE

• In para-jumbles built around an abstract idea, the opening sentence is usually the one stating the broadest, most general claim (here, about the mind's resourcefulness), while the concluding sentence usually contains a summarising or "as if" / "therefore" type statement.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The Emperor was considered as a wicked man.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Virtuous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Wicked" means evil or morally wrong in a very unpleasant or harmful way. (दुष्ट/पापी)

• "Virtuous" means having or showing high moral standards; morally good and righteous — the direct opposite of "wicked". (सदाचारी/सद्गुणी)
◦ Example: He was praised by all as a virtuous and honest ruler.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Savage (क्रूर): Fierce, violent, and uncontrolled; this is actually close in meaning to "wicked" rather than its opposite.

• Option 3: Fierce (उग्र): Having or displaying an intense or ferocious aggressiveness; again a near-synonym of "wicked", not an antonym.

• Option 4: Vile (घृणित): Extremely unpleasant or morally bad; this is also a synonym of "wicked", not its opposite.

NOTE

• All three incorrect options (Savage, Fierce, Vile) are near-synonyms of "wicked" — a common SSC trap in antonym questions is including words that mean almost the same as the given word to mislead candidates who read carelessly.

• Other antonym pairs for "wicked" commonly tested: wicked × noble, wicked × benevolent, wicked × righteous.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. It's because the 'practical people' in society boast of having a practical approach to life.
B. It is very likely for youngsters to seek advice from their elders.
C. Emphasising upon the times that prevailed, the youth very much get their queries answered systematically.
D. In the similar context even the elders are, in most likelihood, expected to give their advice as a word of guidance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. BDCA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence B opens the paragraph, introducing the topic — youngsters seeking advice from their elders.

• Sentence D follows naturally, continuing the same idea from the elders' side — that they too are expected to give advice as guidance, signalled by the phrase "In the similar context", which links back directly to B.

• Sentence C then adds that, emphasising the prevailing times, the youth get their queries answered systematically — a continuation of the advice-giving process described in B and D.

• Sentence A concludes by explaining the reason behind this reliance on "practical people" and their practical approach to life, closing the argument with "It's because...".

• Reading in order: B → D → C → A gives a coherent paragraph.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 (BDCA).

Additional Information

• Option 2 (CDAB) is incorrect because it opens with C, which refers to "the youth" getting queries answered — a detail that only makes sense after B has introduced the idea of youngsters seeking advice.

• Option 3 (ACDB) is incorrect because it opens with the concluding, explanatory sentence A ("It's because...") before the topic it explains has even been introduced.

• Option 4 (DCAB) is incorrect because it opens with D, whose phrase "In the similar context" clearly requires a preceding sentence (B) to refer back to.

NOTE

• Sentences containing phrases like "In the similar context", "It's because", or pronouns referring back to a noun almost never open a paragraph — they are strong clues to eliminate wrong starting options quickly in para-jumble questions.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Matching
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Resembling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Matching" means corresponding or being similar to something else in appearance, quality, or character. (मिलता-जुलता)

• "Resembling" means having a similar appearance or characteristics to something/someone else — very close in meaning to "matching". (समान दिखना)
◦ Example: She wore a scarf resembling/matching the colour of her dress.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Appointing (नियुक्त करना): Assigning a job or role to someone; unrelated to similarity.

• Option 2: Distinguishing (अंतर करना): Recognising or treating something as different; this is actually opposite in sense to "matching".

• Option 3: Adoring (पूजा करना/अत्यधिक प्रेम करना): Loving and admiring someone/something deeply; unrelated to the idea of similarity.

NOTE

• Be careful with "Distinguishing", which is a frequently used distractor in synonym questions because it sounds like it could relate to identification/comparison, but it actually means noting a difference, the opposite of "matching/resembling".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Derision
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Admiration.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Derision" means contemptuous ridicule or mockery. (उपहास/तिरस्कार)

• "Admiration" means a feeling of respect and warm approval for someone or something — the direct opposite of derision. (प्रशंसा/सम्मान)
◦ Example: Instead of derision, his brave act earned him the admiration of the whole town.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Disintegration (विघटन): The process of breaking up into small parts; unrelated to ridicule or respect.

• Option 2: Termination (समाप्ति): The action of bringing something to an end; unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4: Estimation (अनुमान): A rough calculation or judgement of value/amount; while it can sometimes relate to "opinion of someone", it does not carry the strong positive-respect sense needed to be the opposite of "derision".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Derision" tested in SSC: mockery, scorn, ridicule, contempt. Their opposites include admiration, respect, esteem, regard.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.
He was offered a __________(moderate) price for his bungalow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. reasonable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Moderate" means average in amount, intensity, quality, or degree; not extreme or excessive. (मध्यम/उचित)

• "Reasonable", when describing a price, means fair and moderate, not too high or too low — the closest synonym of "moderate" in this context. (उचित)
◦ Example: The shop sells good quality clothes at a reasonable price.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: sustainable (टिकाऊ): Able to be maintained at a certain level, or causing little or no damage to the environment; unrelated to the idea of a fair price.

• Option 2: considerable (काफी/उल्लेखनीय): Notably large in size, amount, or extent — this suggests a large price, which is the opposite of "moderate".

• Option 3: respectable (सम्मानजनक): Regarded by society to be good, proper, or correct; can describe a decent amount but does not specifically carry the "fair, not excessive" sense of "moderate" as precisely as "reasonable" does.

NOTE

• Commonly tested near-synonyms of "moderate/reasonable" in SSC vocabulary: fair, modest, average, temperate — and its antonyms: excessive, exorbitant, extravagant.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
The salesman yielded to the demands of his corrupt boss.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Conceded.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Yielded" (here) means gave in to, or submitted to, a demand or pressure. (झुक जाना/मान लेना)

• "Conceded" means admitted defeat or gave in/agreed to something, typically after resistance — very close in meaning to "yielded" in this context. (स्वीकार कर लेना)
◦ Example: After much argument, she finally conceded/yielded to her colleague's request.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Courted (आकर्षित करने का प्रयास करना): To try to win someone's favour, or to engage in a romantic relationship; unrelated to giving in to demands.

• Option 3: Hounded (परेशान करना): To persistently pursue or harass someone; this describes the person applying the pressure, not the person giving in.

• Option 4: Trended (रुझान दिखाना): To develop in a general direction, or to be popular on social media; unrelated in meaning to "yielded".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "yield" (in the sense of submitting) commonly tested in SSC: submit, capitulate, surrender, comply, acquiesce.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

◦ Example: Please keep the receipt in case you need to return the item.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Deceived" — correctly spelt; means misled or tricked someone. Note it follows the standard "i before e except after c" rule (D-E-C-E-I-V-E-D).

• Option 3: "Resistance" — correctly spelt; means the refusal to accept or comply with something, ending in "-ance" not "-ence".

• Option 4: "Postponed" — correctly spelt; means rearranged for a later time.

NOTE

• The "i before e except after c" rule has notable exceptions in English, including "weird", "seize", "either", "foreign" — words that keep "ei" even without a preceding "c".

• Other commonly confused silent-letter words in SSC spelling questions: "receive", "deceit", "conceit" (all follow "ei" after "c"), and "achieve", "believe", "relief" (all follow "ie" elsewhere).

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Learning a new language can be challenging, but it's also (1)__________. It can open up new opportunities for communication and cultural exchange. When learning a new language, it's important to be patient and (2)__________ yourself time to progress. One way to make language learning easier is to (3)__________ to it every day, even if it's just for a few minutes. This helps in building consistency and reinforces what you're learning. Practising speaking and listening is also important, not just reading and writing. By immersing yourself in the language and culture, you can accelerate your (4)__________ and gain a deeper understanding of the language. Learning a new language is not only practical, but it's also (5)__________ and can be a fun experience.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. rewarding.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Learning a new language can be challenging, but it's also ________." The connector "but" signals a contrast with "challenging" — the missing word must express something positive that offsets the difficulty.

• "Rewarding" means providing satisfaction or worthwhile benefits/results, which fits perfectly as a positive contrast to "challenging".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "insignificant" means unimportant or of little value — this does not form a logical contrast with "challenging"; a challenging task being "insignificant" makes little sense in context.

• Option 3: "pointless" means having no purpose — this is a negative word and cannot contrast positively with "challenging"; the passage overall presents learning a language favourably.

• Option 4: "customising" means adapting something to suit an individual's requirements — it does not fit the sentence sense at all, describing how learning a language "is".

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read beyond the blank to check the tone of the surrounding sentences (here, the next sentence talks about "new opportunities", confirming that a positive word like "rewarding" is required).

solution_text:

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "it's important to be patient and ________ yourself time to progress." The fixed expression "give yourself time" means to allow oneself sufficient time to do or achieve something.

• The verb "give" correctly completes this common collocation "give (someone) time (to do something)".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "neglect" means to fail to care for or give attention to; "neglect yourself time" is not a meaningful or grammatical collocation.

• Option 3: "rush" means to move or act with urgent speed; "rush yourself time" does not make sense and actually contradicts the idea of being "patient" in the same sentence.

• Option 4: "force" means to compel by physical or other means; "force yourself time" is not idiomatic English and does not fit the sense of allowing time.

NOTE

• Collocations like "give yourself time", "take your time", and "allow yourself time" are commonly tested in SSC cloze passages — always check which verb naturally pairs with "time" in context.

solution_text:

• The sentence reads: "By immersing yourself in the language and culture, you can accelerate your ________ and gain a deeper understanding of the language." The verb "accelerate" means to increase the speed of something, and it naturally pairs with "progress" (advancement or development).

• "Accelerate your progress" is a common, meaningful collocation meaning "to advance/improve more quickly".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "pitch" refers to the level or degree of something (e.g., sound pitch), or a sales pitch; "accelerate your pitch" does not fit the context of language learning.

• Option 2: "complacency" means a feeling of smug self-satisfaction, often leading to a lack of effort; it is a negative trait, and it would not make logical sense to "accelerate" complacency as a benefit of immersion.

• Option 4: "stamina" means physical or mental endurance/staying power; while immersion could arguably build endurance, it does not fit as naturally as "progress" with the phrase "gain a deeper understanding of the language" that follows.

NOTE

• The collocation "accelerate progress" is a standard phrase in educational/self-improvement contexts and is commonly tested in SSC cloze passages.
